canonical_name: Floquet theorem for fundamental matrices of periodic linear systems (catalog family; exact proposition open)
literal_source_claim_zh: 周期系统的基本解矩阵
literal_source_claim_en: fundamental matrix of a periodic system
candidate_family_not_credited_as_stateme: For a source-selected scalar or first-order periodic linear differential system, prove the source-selected monodromy identity, Floquet factorization, constant-coefficient reduction, or exact conjunction for its normalized or arbitrary fundamental matrices, with every coefficient, field, period, regularity, invertibility, logarithm, uniqueness, and boundary convention fixed by that source.
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies only 'fundamental matrix of a periodic system'. It does not choose scalar versus first-order system, coefficient regularity, field, positive period, solution and fundamental-matrix predicates, normalization, multiplication orientation, monodromy identity versus exponential-periodic factorization or reduction, complex versus real factors, period T versus 2T, logarithm hypotheses, uniqueness, binders, or boundary cases. Selecting a familiar formulation would add proposition-changing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted source must fix scalar or system form, time domain, finite dimension, real or complex scalar field, topology and norms, coefficient and solution types, and all universes and typeclass assumptions.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not choose a monodromy/quasiperiodicity identity, exponential-periodic Floquet factorization, constant-coefficient reduction, Floquet-solution basis, or conjunction of these conclusions.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no proposition is selected; every listed dimension, period, coefficient, monodromy, logarithm, normalization, and base-time case must be resolved by the statement phase.
candidate_scope_not_credited: the normalized fundamental-matrix identity Phi(t+T)=Phi(t)Phi(T) for a continuous period-T coefficient
a complex Floquet factorization Phi(t)=P(t) exp(tB) with period-T invertible P and constant B
a real factorization allowing period 2T or imposing source-specific real-logarithm hypotheses
reduction of the periodic system to a constant-coefficient system by an invertible periodic change of variables
a scalar higher-order periodic equation transported to a companion first-order system
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: dimension zero, the zero coefficient, a constant coefficient, and identity monodromy
period zero, negative periods, nonminimal periods, and whether positivity is explicit
singular candidate solution matrices and the exact pointwise invertibility requirement
real monodromy matrices without a real logarithm and the period-doubling alternative
normalization at zero versus another base time and resulting monodromy conjugacy
uniqueness or gauge freedom in the periodic and constant factors
excluded_substitutions: THM-M-1352 Floquet theory used as a broader replacement for this target
THM-M-1354 characteristic exponents or THM-M-1355 linear-system stability used as the root
a periodicity definition, matrix-exponential invertibility, or ODE existence result presented as Floquet's theorem
a scalar, constant-coefficient, one-dimensional, complex-only, or normalized special case silently substituted for a broader selected source
a structure field or hypothesis that assumes the monodromy identity, logarithm, factorization, periodic factor, or reduction
numerical trajectories, sampled monodromy, floating-point spectra, or the untrusted catalog status used as proof evidence
